clue.text: Don't continue if scared

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bring something to a close, as an instruction

definitions.note: the phrase is 'have the wind up', so the answer names the fear rather than describing a person
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the state of fright in the phrase 'to have the ... '

explanation.surface: Advice to someone losing their nerve: if frightened, stop going on.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'have the wind up' is British slang for being frightened, while to wind something up is to finish it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means finish or conclude, and the noun phrase in British slang means a fit of nerves or fright.

clue.text: Smooth metal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: press creases out of clothes
second meaning: the chemical element Fe

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of a polished metal; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means press creases out of fabric; as a noun it is a common magnetic element used for steel.

clue.text: Rush to get on the panel

parts.note: to dash is to rush
to board a train or ship is to get on it

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying to join a committee or panel of judges.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's instrument panel in front of the driver carries the speedometer, fuel gauge and other dials.

clue.text: Author to have a shot at verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
to have a shot is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: A prose writer deciding to try his hand at writing poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is writing in metrical lines, the general term for poems as a form of literature.

clue.text: Complete section of boxing match cancelled

parts.note: a boxing bout is divided into rounds
an event that is called off is cancelled

explanation.surface: A boxing contest abandoned partway through one of its rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish something off neatly, giving it a final touch, is to bring it to completion.

clue.text: Using coarse expressions, more or less

definitions.meaning: literal reading: talking in a crude or rough way

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase describes crude talk; as an idiom it means approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom signals an approximation, just as the phrase about quantity does; literally it describes rough, vulgar talk.

clue.text: Took off some weight?

parts.note: surface reading: lost a few pounds by dieting
setter's reading: removed a burden or cargo from a lorry or ship

explanation.walkthrough: The dieting sense is the trap; the weight is a load being taken off a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the cargo or burden from a vehicle or animal is emptying it of its freight.

clue.text: Cord I twisted into a sort of column

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of its original shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone winding a piece of string around a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, the plainest style of pillar and capital.

clue.text: It springs to hand in attack

definitions.text: It springs to hand in attack

parts.words: It springs to hand in attack
parts.note: surface reading: something that leaps readily into use when fighting
setter's reading: a weapon whose blade flies out on a spring when a button is pressed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Springs' sounds like quick readiness, but it is literal: the blade is spring-loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: This weapon is a pocket blade released by a spring at the press of a button, often used by street attackers.

clue.text: Underwater explorer to cause commotion at university

indicators.note: a commotion is a disturbance, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A diver turning up on campus and stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Cousteau was the French oceanographer who co-invented the aqualung.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Cousteau was the celebrated French naval officer and filmmaker who explored the oceans and pioneered scuba diving.

clue.text: A poet not out after a frolic

indicators.note: after tells us the not-out piece is placed following the frolic piece

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or a frolic
in cricket a batsman not out is still in

explanation.surface: A cricketing poet still batting after some fun on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Larkin was an English poet, librarian in Hull, author of 'The Whitsun Weddings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was a twentieth-century English writer of verse, known for collections such as High Windows.

clue.text: It's eaten at an age-old celebration

definitions.text: It's eaten at an age-old celebration

parts.note: surface reading: a feast with ancient traditions
setter's reading: a party marking how old someone has become

explanation.walkthrough: 'Age-old' suggests something ancient, but read as 'age' plus 'old' it is a party for turning a year older.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle-topped sweet bake is cut and eaten at the annual party marking someone's age.

clue.text: Not against upsetting an opponent

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Not wanting to oppose someone for fear of upsetting a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not against' sounds like support, yet the word it makes is the reverse of support.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary or rival in a contest or story is someone who struggles against another.

clue.text: Order a gin for Swedish girl

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are put into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Buying a gin at the bar for a young woman from Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common Scandinavian female first name, which crosswords define by nationality and sex.

clue.text: Submissive bearing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: giving way to pressure or others
second meaning: producing crops or fruit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a noun for demeanour, but it means producing, as land produces a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone who gives way easily, and also land or trees that produce a harvest.

clue.text: Banked left

definitions.meaning: first meaning: paid money into an account
second meaning: set down and placed somewhere

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction, partnering the turn an aircraft makes when it banks.
explanation.definitionFit: It means paid money into an account, and also laid something down, as a river lays silt.

clue.text: Press men in China

definitions.meaning: first meaning: force men into service as sailors

definitions.note: a place in China rather than a word meaning China
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the great port city

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press men' looks like reporters, but to press men is to force them into naval service.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapping men to serve as sailors is named after the Chinese port, which is also the largest city in that country.

clue.text: An iron-clad reason for not buying luxuries?

definitions.text: An iron-clad reason for not buying luxuries?

parts.note: surface reading: a watertight, unbreakable reason
setter's reading: an armoured vessel, read as a tough boat

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer and it is a tough vessel, which is what an ironclad warship is; whole, it means poverty that rules out luxuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Privation or financial suffering is exactly the condition that stops people spending on treats.

clue.text: Pastry promotion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a light flaky dough
second meaning: exaggerated praise used for advertising

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like an advertising campaign for baked goods; they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light flaky dough, and also an overblown piece of advertising or praise for a product.

clue.text: He turns up in the country

definitions.text: He turns up in the country

parts.words: He turns up in the country
parts.note: surface reading: a man who arrives in the countryside
setter's reading: a man who turns over the soil on a farm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' looks like arriving, but it means ploughing the soil over.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer who cultivates and ploughs the land is one who works the soil, turning it over.

clue.text: They may be running the moment race is organised

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Athletes off and running as soon as the race is set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests athletes, but it belongs to the phrase for live spoken description of an event.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters give a running description of sporting events as they unfold, live and continuous.

clue.text: Means of communication for a TV detective

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the code of dots and dashes
second meaning: the Oxford inspector in the ITV series

explanation.surface: A police officer on television using some way of getting in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of the long-running British TV drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The telegraph code of dots and dashes shares its name with Colin Dexter's Oxford inspector, famous from television.

clue.text: Brickbats aimed at military aircraft?

definitions.note: describes the fire itself; the answer is a noun

explanation.surface: Bricks being hurled at warplanes overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Brickbats are thrown missiles and so criticism; the second meaning is the shells fired up at planes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from a German anti-aircraft gun and figuratively means hostile criticism directed at someone.

clue.text: Boatman returns to old address

indicators.note: returns means comes back the way it went, so the name is read from the end

parts.note: Harris is one of the three men in Jerome K Jerome's novel Three Men in a Boat

explanation.surface: A rower heading back to a former home.
explanation.walkthrough: Address here means a form of address, a way of speaking to someone, not a house.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic contemptuous form used when speaking to a man or boy of lower status.

clue.text: The converse of indolence?

parts.note: surface reading: the opposite of laziness
setter's reading: conversation that comes from being lazy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Converse' seems to mean opposite, but here it is the noun for conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip or chatter without purpose is conversation of an unoccupied, lazy kind.

clue.text: Giving speech, don't start being inaudible

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is left off the word

parts.note: muttering is speaking too low to be heard clearly

explanation.surface: Advice to a nervous speaker not to begin by mumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice words or sounds aloud from the mouth is to express them in speech.

clue.text: Heavenly sight delightful to shepherds

parts.note: surface reading: a divine vision, as shepherds saw angels
setter's reading: the weather proverb about the evening sky

explanation.walkthrough: The nativity angels are the trap; the rhyme is 'at night, shepherd's delight', promising fine weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson evening sky foretells good weather in the old rhyme, which says it pleases those who tend flocks.
